title: Sen. Rick Scott introduces bill to expedite federal review of state wildlife plans
text:
Sen. Rick Scott introduces bill to expedite federal review of state wildlife plans
U.S. Senator Rick Scott introduced the Make State Wildlife Action Plan Efficient Act on Aug. 5, requiring the U.S. Department of the Interior to act on state conservation efforts within 180 days of submission.
States submit annual State Wildlife Action Plans to the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, outlining which non-game species require intervention so they do not become threatened or endangered. Currently, there is no deadline for federal approval, which can delay funding for conservation needs by a year or more.
In December 2025, Congressman Byron Donalds’ companion legislation passed the House of Representatives.
Scott said, “Florida’s natural beauty, including its wildlife, is worth protecting. It is unacceptable that federal bureaucracy stalls critical wildlife funding year after year, leaving Florida’s wildlife and our environment vulnerable. The American people deserve prompt and efficient use of their tax dollars. I’m glad to join Congressman Donalds to fast-track this funding and protect Florida’s wildlife.”
Donalds said, “When states do the work to protect wildlife, Washington should do its part by reviewing their plans on time. Giving agencies 180 days to act will help cut through red tape and ensure states can keep protecting the wildlife and natural resources their communities depend on. I am grateful to Senator Scott for joining this effort to get the bill across the finish line.”
Scott champions fiscal responsibility and policies supporting families and small businesses; he served in the U.S. Navy aboard USS Glover after high school; he earned degrees from University of Missouri-Kansas City and Southern Methodist University; he serves on several Senate committees; was elected as senator representing Florida; and with his wife Ann has raised two daughters, according to his official website.
